t: A kingdom on the northern shore of Lake Victoria that rose from a small state to the dominant power of the Great Lakes by 1800.
Its kabakas ruled through appointed chiefs, with a council, a chief minister and a fleet of war canoes on the lake.
Buganda gave its name to Uganda; abolished in 1967, the monarchy was restored as a cultural institution in 1993.
dyk: Because princes belonged to their mothers’ clans, the Ganda royal family had no clan of its own, and any clan could hope to provide a future kabaka.
ev: Kabakas Junju and Semakookiro conquer the province of Buddu from Bunyoro
John Hanning Speke reaches the court of Mutesa I
The first Protestant missionaries arrive in Buganda
Christian converts are executed at Namugongo on the orders of Mwanga II
Protestants defeat Catholics at the Battle of Mengo
The Buganda Agreement makes the kingdom a privileged part of the Uganda Protectorate
Troops under Idi Amin storm the kabaka’s palace at Mengo
Uganda’s new constitution abolishes the kingdoms

f.capital: Royal capitals moved with each reign; later Mengo (Kampala)
